national.title: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
national.summary: Six people were killed in the shooting, and three bodies of the suspect's family members were found at their home.
national.body:
A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say.

The 24-year-old was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday, and died early on Monday morning, police said.

Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.

Officials initially reported the gunman had apparently been inspired by "far-right ideologies", but have since said they are still investigating any possible motivation.

After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man. He has not yet been officially named.

In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.

However, during a press briefing on Monday morning, Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, said investigations into his motive remain ongoing.

Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack.

national.title: Trump says he sees no reason to escalate war with Iran
national.summary: President Trump told 60 Minutes the war with Iran was a "good decision" in the long term, despite its short-term impact.
national.body: The price of Brent crude oil, the international standard, fell 2% early Monday morning to $96.38 per barrel, continuing a downward trend seen for more than a week as markets appeared to take hope from President Trump casting doubt on a return to full-scale war with Iran. U.S. benchmark crude also fell, down 1.5% early Monday to $89.56 per barrel. Oil prices have been up significantly since the U.S. and Israel launched the war with Iran, and Iran responded by attacking and threatening commercial ships in the key energy supply routes of the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. They remain about 50% higher than a year ago, before the war began, but down from highs seen during the peak of fighting, when Brent crude soared to near $120 a barrel.

national.title: U.S. girl shot dead by police during cartel chase in Mexico
national.summary: The state prosecutor's office said that Aranza, a 7-year-old who was born in the United States, was hit in the head by police gunfire.
national.body: Mexican police shot dead a 7-year-old American girl when they opened fire on her family's vehicle from a helicopter during a drug enforcement operation, the state prosecutor confirmed Friday. Police captured a local criminal in Matamoros, which borders Brownsville, Texas, on October 29, triggering a series of street blockades by gunmen in the area. The Tamaulipas state prosecutor's office said Friday that Aranza, a 7-year-old who was born in the United States, was hit in the head by police gunfire. The girl's mother told Mexican media she was traveling with five children and her husband in a pickup truck when they noticed a police helicopter was following them. She said the family stopped the vehicle and her husband got out to say they were civilians with children but they were fired at anyway. Tamaulipas Attorney General Jesus Govea told Mexico's Milenio network the officers were responding to "an attack they allegedly came under" from the ground during the roadblocks. The officers who opened fire remain free but "significant progress is being made in the course of the investigation," Govea said.KABB-TV in San Antonio reported that the violence erupted following the arrest of Alfredo Cárdenas Rodríguez, an alleged high-ranking member of the Ciclones faction of the Gulf Cartel.Mexico's Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said on social media that Cárdenas Rodríguez – also known as "Axel" -- was a linked to homicides, kidnappings, extortion and trafficking drugs, weapons and people into the United States.The U.S. Consulate in Matamoros said at the time that it issued a shelter-in-place order for employees following the law enforcement operation. Numerous civilians have died in the crossfire of drug-related violence in Mexico over the past two decades.In 2024, human rights activists and relatives in the Mexican border city of Nuevo Laredo, across from Laredo, Texas, blamed the army and National Guard troops in the deaths of a nurse and an 8-year-old girl. The relatives said that the victims were apparently caught in the crossfire of gun battles with suspected drug cartel vehicles being pursued by military patrols.

national.title: At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal
national.summary: The Atlantic crossing to Spain's Canary Islands remains dangerous for migrants seeking a better life
national.body:
At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source.

The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established.

The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands.

Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors.

Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued.

President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings.

In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys.

"We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said.

national.title: Democrats won big on issues like immigration. But ICE still has the money
national.summary: Following Tuesday's "blue wave," Democrats have vowed to reign in ICE's power. What could they actually accomplish?
national.body:
In the days leading up to the midterm elections, hundreds of people left their "I voted" stickers on a memorial for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo , a Houston man killed by federal immigration agents earlier this year.

"The fact that people were thinking of my dad and thinking of other immigrants — that just means the world to me," said Ronaldo Salgado, Salgado Araujo's son, told NPR.

Those votes resulted in a seismic political shift in Texas: for the first time, a Latina, Democrat Gina Hinojosa , will be governor. Texans also elected the state's first Democratic U.S. senator in nearly 40 years, and the Texas House of Representatives flipped .

"Unfortunately, Texas has become like the epicenter of ICE enforcement and like gross violence against immigrants," Ronaldo Salgado said. "Well, the voters have spoken — incoming lawmakers now have a duty to listen to us."

Politics A judge blocked construction of Trump's arch at the 11th hour. What's next? Immigration policy was one of the top issues on voters' minds this election, according to exit polling . Artemio Muñiz of the Texas Federation of Hispanic Republicans, told NPR "with these anti-immigrant-type policies, I think the Hispanic community got fed up."

That seems more true than ever in the counties along the U.S.-Mexico border, which flipped Democratic after supporting Trump in 2024.

"I think the message is clear from the Texas Hispanic community that the only acceptable or effective Hispanic outreach from the Republican Party in Texas is one that includes a reasonable solution for immigration," Muñiz said, suggesting the solution should include secured borders and a legal pathway for undocumented immigrants who have been in the U.S. for decades.

In Texas, Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa is facing calls to end the state's partnership with ICE.

national.title: Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill?
national.summary: Affordability concerns were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as tariffs and the war in Iran drove up prices, including food costs. Now, Americans are expecting relief from Washington.
national.body:
It's been a feature of campaign ads and stump speeches for months: grocery prices are out of control.

Congress After sweeping midterm wins, here's what Democrats hope to get done in the majority Affordability concerns, including high food costs, were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as the Trump administration's tariffs and the war in Iran continued to drive up prices. That economic strain helped Democrats win control of both houses of Congress on Tuesday.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said the incoming majority would make tackling high prices a priority come January. "It was a tremendous victory for the American people and a strong rebuke of MAGA extremism, which has made life more expensive for everyday Americans despite their promises to lower the high cost of living on day one," he told NPR on Friday.

The question is how Democrats will do that with President Trump still in the Oval Office, willing to wield his veto pen. Senate Democrats won't have a filibuster-proof majority, and Trump may have little appetite to roll back his signature tariffs or reverse course on the Iran war, two of the main causes of high food prices.

Lael Brainard, who leads a public policy group called The Kitchen Table Project, said Americans are nevertheless expecting relief from Washington — and quickly.

"They are feeling like they are getting squeezed by high prices that don't need to be that high," she said.

Despite the political hurdles, Democrats said they intend to move ahead with plans to cut grocery bills, including by rolling back Trump's tariffs. Those tariffs have not only raised the cost of certain foods and drinks imported to the U.S., but also created other pressures on the food industry by making it more expensive to import things like machine parts and packaging.

Consider This from NPR Affordability is a top issue this election cycle. How is it shaping what voters do? The Iran war has led to a surge in energy prices, which has made it more expensive to transport just about everything. Fertilizer costs also grew when the closure of the Strait of Hormuz cut off a significant portion of the global fertilizer trade.

national.title: On wild Cumberland Island, a land swap proposal stirs controversy
national.summary: Visitors, ecologists, park rangers and residents all love this wild barrier island off the coast of southern Georgia. But they have different ideas of how to best protect it.
national.body:
A wild horse grazes on whatever food it can find on Cumberland Island, Ga. on Oct 8, 2026. The National Park Service, which has managed the island since 1972, recently proposed a land swap with descendants of Thomas Carnegie, the wealthy Gilded Age industrialist who built homes on the island. Malcolm Jackson for NPR hide caption

CUMBERLAND ISLAND, Ga.— Wild horses, feral hogs and deer roam free on this 18-mile barrier island, one of the largest and most ecologically diverse along the Atlantic coast. The landscape includes salt marshes, maritime forests, and an expansive stretch of pristine, untouched beach only accessible to the public by ferry.

Since 1972, the National Park Service has managed Cumberland Island National Seashore, including roughly 9,800 acres of wilderness designated by an act of Congress which stated that "the seashore shall be permanently preserved in its primitive state."

But there's more on this island than federally protected wilderness. Visitors also can find Native-American relics, remnants of Spanish missions, the ruins of ante-bellum plantations, and opulent homes built by the wealthy Gilded Age industrialist Thomas Carnegie and his wife Lucy, who had 9 children.

Descendants of the Carnegies still live or vacation here on private property, and the park service has proposed a land swap with them that would allow for new construction. That possibility is creating tension between the many stakeholders who all have differing views of what it means to preserve the island they hold dear.

Park superintendent Melissa Trenchik has been defending the plan, giving media tours to an area under a grove of huge live oak trees on Cumberland's west side, which overlooks an expansive salt marsh and Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay on the horizon.

It is currently parkland, which under the proposal would be handed over to two branches of Carnegie descendants for the construction of up to eight new private homes.

A portion of the maritime forest that's part of the proposed land swap. Malcolm Jackson for NPR hide caption

national.title: Nebraska rushed Medicaid work rules. Then a cancer patient was told he'd lost coverage
national.summary: Health clinics and organizations advocating for poor and working-class Nebraskans say the rollout of Medicaid work requirements has been rife with problems.
national.body:
Shortly after being diagnosed with kidney cancer, Eli McCreary of Omaha, Neb., was told by a hospital that he'd lost his Medicaid coverage. Chris Machian/KFF Health News hide caption

Eli McCreary of Omaha, Neb., said he had recently been diagnosed with kidney cancer when he got a call from a local hospital run by CHI Health. He said he was informed that he wasn't insured anymore under Medicaid — and that the hospital would cancel his appointments unless he paid out-of-pocket.

McCreary, who was 64 at the time, said he phoned a call center for help. He said he was told his benefits under Medicaid, the government health program for people with low incomes or disabilities, now required that he have a job.

"You're required to do work to stay on," McCreary said a representative told him. "And you haven't fulfilled your work requirement."

Health Reporting in the States Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on Oct 1. Patients are confused For decades, McCreary said, he has battled drug addiction. A substance use treatment program discharged him in March, and in June he was diagnosed with cancer in his right kidney, according to documents reviewed by KFF Health News. He also has diabetes and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

"I don't understand what job I can get," McCreary said. "I can't walk. I can hardly breathe. I can't move around. What job am I going to get?"

McCreary said he canceled a CT scan and other tests at the hospital, which is part of CommonSpirit Health, the nation's largest Catholic health system. He also delayed a cancer-related appointment with a physician who travels back and forth to Omaha. "I missed my window of opportunity with him for another month," he said.

Taylor Miller, a spokesperson for CHI Health, declined to answer questions about McCreary's experience. In an emailed statement, she said that "CHI Health is committed to helping patients understand their health care coverage and access to care, including available financial assistance resources."

national.title: Trump says he was 'kidding' about Dana White press secretary offer
national.summary: The president told the Ultimate Fighting Championship boss to "please take the job" in a Truth Social post on Saturday.
national.body:
US President Donald Trump has said he "was kidding" about asking Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be the White House press secretary.

Trump told the media on Sunday that White "loves the idea" but that the invitation was "just a little fun".

It comes after the president posted on his Truth Social platform on Saturday that he had offered White the role, asking him to take it while writing, "Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other."

White said later that day he was going to meet the president on Monday, but would not be drawn into whether or not he would take the vacant position.

On Sunday Trump told reporters White was visiting him on Monday for "other reasons".

"I think he's going to be in Washington. So he's going to come over and see me.

"I will tell you, I was only kidding. But Dana loves the idea. And there's only one Dana. He's great," the president said.

The press secretary role is yet to be filled after it became vacant in October when Katie Zacharia quit after less than five days in the job .

national.title: Nvidia investigates CEO Jensen Huang over Chinese espionage concerns
national.summary: The board of Nvidia said it had no reason to believe that the company's secrets or national security were compromised.

national.summary: Once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", Huang is mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
national.body:
Jensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures.

He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies.

As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China.

The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US.

He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.

He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Although she had just bought hashish from a drug dealer, the woman decided to call the police.

It was because, along with the illegal drugs, she had been handed a note by the young seller during their brief meeting on a Marseille housing estate in 2022.

"We're being held captive and need help. We are 15-years-old," it read.

The teenage dealer, a French court heard earlier this year, was one of two boys being held by a gang which they had both initially approached looking for paid work - albeit illegal.

One boy had been tasked with handling money, the other worked streets around the Frais-Vallon estate. Soon though, bosses had accused them of being responsible for "shortfalls" in takings.

What followed were regular beatings, the court was told, and being forced to dance naked in front of a camera as a form of blackmail. One of the boys was also raped.

Hours after the woman was passed the note, the two teenagers had tried to escape from a second-storey window, injuring themselves in the process. One managed to get away, while the other was caught, beaten and stabbed, but survived.

national.title: Pope delivers veiled rebuke of Milei's austerity measures
national.summary: Pope Leo made the comments as he arrived in Argentina on the second leg of his Latin America tour.
national.body:
Pope Leo XIV has said Argentina's economy must benefit everyone including the poor, in a diplomatic but pointed critique of President Javier Milei's austerity measures.

The Pope was speaking as he arrived in Buenos Aires, the second stop on a 12-day tour of Latin America, only three weeks after having had surgery for lung cancer.

In response, right-wing leader Milei said his government was working to avoid "punishing the Argentines of tomorrow in order to benefit the Argentines of today".

This leg of the Pope's journey was expected be the most politically sensitive, with the president's agenda of slashing public spending having been denounced by the Catholic Church for hitting the poorest hardest.

"The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy," Pope Leo said.

He stressed the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs", and urged that "particular concern be shown for those affected by illness, dependency and disability" - a veiled reference to the government's controversial cuts to disability assistance.

In what appeared to be a rebuke of Milei's combative style and language, the Pope said strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words".

Milei had been particularly outspoken about Leo's predecessor Pope Francis, whom he called "evil on earth" and a "communist" for promoting a doctrine of social justice to help the poor.

national.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued from sea after nine hours in Pacific Ocean
national.summary: Two US fishermen say they spotted the man treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast.
national.body:
A cruise ship pianist was found treading water around 20 miles (32km) off the Californian coast after falling overboard, according to US media reports.

Two fishermen discovered the Royal Caribbean employee near Catalina Island on Friday and officials believe he may have been in the Pacific Ocean for nine hours, according to CBS News, the BBC's US news partner.

"I'm like, 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat; let's get all of our lines in," Grant Garrett was quoted as saying, recalling the moment he and Sean Norton spotted him.

The man, who has not yet been identified, was taken to hospital in a stable condition, the US Coast Guard told the BBC, adding it was investigating the incident.

The fishermen say the man identified himself as a pianist on a 14-deck cruise ship called the Ovation of the Seas.

"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said.

The Coast Guard said in a statement it had received a report from "a Good Samaritan who recovered a conscious individual from the water".

The person was handed over to Newport Beach Lifeguards, who confirmed he was an employee of the Ovation of the Seas cruise ship, it said.

New York congressman Hakeem Jeffries told ABC's programme This Week that Hegseth had "abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran".

The massive artificial intelligence chip maker Nvidia says it is launching an internal investigation, after reports that the company's CEO was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the statement from the company's board of directors reads in part.

The Times released a series of reports over the last two weeks detailing Huang's alleged relationship with a woman named Alice Huang, who is accused of being a spy for China. The two are not related. NPR has reached out to the Chinese Embassy in Washington, D.C. but has not received a response.

"The so-called Chinese spy allegation is groundless," Guo Jiakun, a spokesman for China's foreign ministry told reporters in a regular briefing. "It is nothing but a smear against China."

"Alice Huang is a Chinese national. She's a Chinese businesswoman who had something of a mysterious and meteoric rise," Times reporter Ana Swanson explained on NPR's technology podcast Machine Gods .

Alice Huang ran a Singapore-based company that purchased nearly $5 billion in Nvidia chip technology, Swanson says. "At the same time, she was also seen personally with Jensen Huang on a couple of occasions after some industry events in Taiwan. They were photographed together both at a bar with other suppliers and then also out to dinner with some other executives."

local.title: NY Gov. Hochul won with a mandate from voters. But what was the message?
local.summary: The nationwide blue wave was seen as a repudiation of President Trump.
local.body:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul scored the type of political victory on Election Day that typically comes with a mandate — but what message voters were trying to send depends on who you ask.

The Democratic governor topped her Republican opponent Bruce Blakeman by about 20 percentage points, or 1.2 million votes, tripling her margin of victory from the last time she ran in 2022. She increased her vote share in every single one of New York’s 62 counties, in red and blue areas alike, and won eight counties she lost four years ago — including Nassau, where Blakeman is county executive.

But what, exactly, does that result tell us about what voters are expecting from Hochul in her second full term? Everyone seems to have a different answer.

Christina Greer, a Fordham University political science professor, said the blue wave that swept the nation on Election Day — which saw Democrats win key races in traditionally Republican states — makes a New York-specific mandate difficult to define.

“I'm not sure if the governor has a mandate, and I think this goes for not just Kathy Hochul, but a lot of the Democrats who were successful on Tuesday,” she said. “I think we need to be careful as to: Is it a vote for Kathy Hochul, or is it a vote against Donald Trump?”

Hochul’s campaign also focused on tying Blakeman to Trump, his friend and ally who headlined a rally in Syracuse just before voters started casting their ballots. Her ads frequently included a clip of Blakeman saying he would “never be disloyal” to the Republican president.

More than 60% of voters in New York view the president unfavorably, according to recent public opinion polls . Many voters blamed Trump for raising the price of gas through the war in Iran.

“ The Democrat message last night was basically, ’We’re not him,’” said Republican political consultant Mike Dawidziak. “And that message worked last night, but it’s not gonna work in two years.”

NEW ORLEANS (AP) -- Saints second-year quarterback Tyler Shough likes to think he has a refined and thoughtful approach to remaining calm and in control in the clutch.

He backed it up against the Cleveland Browns and fellow second-year QB Shedeur Sanders on Sunday.

Shough floated a 15-yard timing pass to Juwan Johnson toward the right corner of the end zone for a touchdown for New Orleans in overtime, and the desperate Saints stopped a do-or-die, 2-point conversion to hold on, 23-22.

“We go down to the end of the game, he gets better and better,” Saints receiver Chris Olave said of Shough. “He’s calm and collected and we’ve got the utmost confidence in Tyler.”

After the Saints (3-5) scored on the first possession of overtime, Cleveland answered when Harold Fannin Jr. turned a short pass from Sanders into a tackle-breaking, 39-yard touchdown with a minute left in overtime.

The Browns (5-4) opted for a 2-point conversion for the win, but Sanders was forced to roll right under pressure from Carl Granderson and threw incomplete, giving the Saints their first win at home this season.

“We looked at ourself in the mirror and we know what we’ve got to do,” said Granderson, who had two of the Saints’ five sacks. “It’s time to turn this thing around now and we’re excited to get the next one. So, stay tuned.”

Cleveland coach Todd Monken said he never considered kicking the extra point.

CORTLAND -- The historic postseason run of the Fredonia State women’s soccer team came to an end on Saturday as the Blue Devils fell to Cortland 4-1 in the SUNYAC Tournament final at Holloway Field.

The appearance marked the first trip to the conference championship game in program history for Fredonia, which concluded one of the most successful seasons the program has ever enjoyed with a 12-4-4 record. The 12 wins matched a school record previously reached by the 2011, 2012 and 2024 teams.

Gabby Irwin had the lone Devil goal, converting a penalty kick during the 89th minute. Goalkeeper Alyssa Hatch totaled 10 saves. Hatch, Irwin and Makayla Stainbrook were selected to the SUNYAC All-Tournament Team.

Cortland struck first in the 13th minute when Gianna Cirilla headed home a free kick service for a 1-0 lead. The Red Dragons doubled the advantage less than five minutes later as Tyla Vuotto redirected a cross into the net, and Leah Rehm extended the lead to 3-0 with a long-range strike in the 43rd minute.

Cirilla added her second goal of the match in the 87th minute to make it 4-0 before Fredonia answered in the closing moments. After a foul in the penalty area, Irwin converted her PK after she was taken down in the box.

BUFFALO (AP) -- Tomas Hertl scored two goals and the Vegas Golden Knights won their third straight game, 4-1 over the Buffalo Sabres on Sunday.

Hertl scored both of his goals in the third period to help put the game away for the Golden Knights, who finished their road trip 3-0-1.

Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner also scored for Vegas while Adin Hill made 27 saves.

Beck Malenstyn scored and Colten Ellis made 21 saves for Buffalo, which has lost two of its last three games.

Marner opened the scoring with a short-handed goal at 12:17 of the second period following a turnover by Tage Thompson.

Eichel, who was the Sabres first-round draft pick in 2015 and traded to Vegas in 2021, made it 2-0 one minute and 26 seconds later with his eighth goal of the season. He has seven goals and three assists in eight games against Buffalo in his career.

Malenstyn cut the Vegas lead to 2-1 with his first goal on a goalmouth scrum at 4:26 of the third period, but Hertl made it 3-1 just 1:17 later.

MADRID (AP) -- Joe Burrow threw for three touchdowns and rushed for another and the Cincinnati Bengals’ offense kept rolling to defeat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid on Sunday for their fourth straight win.

Ja’Marr Chase had eight receptions for 142 yards in the first half, and Tee Higgins added two touchdown catches at Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium. Chase finished with 10 catches for 155 yards and a touchdown.

After his 47-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, Chase celebrated with Higgins in bullfighting style, with Higgins mimicking a bull by putting his hands on his head and Chase playing the matador with an imaginary cape.

The Bengals (6-2) have scored 30 points or more in four straight games for the first time since 1997. It was the second consecutive defeat for the Falcons (3-6).

Burrow, who completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards Sunday, had thrown five touchdown passes and rushed for another in overtime in the team’s 43-36 win over the Tennessee Titans last week.

MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. (AP) -- Jahmyr Gibbs had a rushing touchdown, Jared Goff threw for 170 yards and Detroit beat Miami for its fourth straight victory.

Jake Bates made four field goals on a day that was a bit underwhelming for Goff and the Lions’ top-ranked offense, which entered averaging 29 points and 395.4 yards per game but finished with 271 yards.

Goff completed 17 of 25 passes while being sacked three times as Miami’s defense pressured him throughout. Goff was intercepted by rookie cornerback Chris Johnson on a tipped pass in the first quarter -- just the second pick he has thrown this season.

local.summary: Bob Winner, the former legendary Clymer Central School boys basketball coach, was laid to rest last Friday morning at a graveside service in Corry, Pennsylvania. He was 90 years old. Dennis Hinsdale, one of Winner’s former players, needed only two words and two syllables to describe his longtime fri
local.body:
OBSERVER File Photo In this February 1993 file photo, Bob Winner holds aloft a commemorative basketball in recognition of his 400th career victory as the boys varsity coach at Clymer Central School.

OBSERVER File Photo In this March 1993 file photo, Clymer boys varsity basketball coach Bob Winner is seen during the Section VI Class D championship game at the University at Buffalo’s Alumni Arena. The Pirates defeated Ripley for the title, 60-53.

Bob Winner, the former legendary Clymer Central School boys basketball coach, was laid to rest last Friday morning at a graveside service in Corry, Pennsylvania. He was 90 years old. Dennis Hinsdale, one of Winner's former players, needed only two words and two syllables to describe his longtime friend: "The best."

"He taught us more about life than just playing basketball," said Hinsdale (Class of 1973).

No one can argue that point, because Winner's influence was felt in all circumstances, not just on game nights.

"I had graduated and he was still the athletic director," Hinsdale recalled. "I said to him, 'Hey, if you ever need a coach, I'd be interested.' He said that he would keep that in mind. ... A year later, he called me and asked if I was still interested because he had an opening."

Years later, Hinsdale coached the Lady Pirates to the 2009-2010 New York State Public High School Athletic Association title.

During his tenure at Clymer, Winner guided the program to seven league championships; four Section VI titles; and posted an overall record of 407-267. His 1972-73 team, which claimed league and sectional crowns, was unbeaten, finishing 20-0.

local.title: WACS hears capital project update, cost concerns
local.summary: Westfield Academy and Central School Board of Education members learned that the district’s Capital Improvement Project is about 57% complete at their meeting this month. WACS Superintendent Ryan Sikorski spoke about the tour of the construction area that he and the board took that very day, led by
local.body:
Westfield Academy and Central School Board of Education members learned that the district’s Capital Improvement Project is about 57% complete at their meeting this month.

WACS Superintendent Ryan Sikorski spoke about the tour of the construction area that he and the board took that very day, led by the architects and project managers. “The progress so far is very impressive,” he said. “The locker rooms will be unveiled in November and the staff and students are excited for that.”

Business Manager Josh Melquist reported that the change orders for the Capital Improvement Project total around $144,000. “This is still well under what was planned for,” he said.

The board approved a Capital Improvement contract with Landscape Structures, Inc. for a new playground. Board member Tom Tarpley said he was disappointed to see that the district would be charged more than a half million dollars. “I feel that the district is being overcharged and taken advantage of,” he said. “I will vote to approve the contract since the project has been voter approved, but the district needs to find a better way in the future to prevent us being unfairly charged.”

Sikorski also told board members that current ex-officio student board members, Liberty Maring and Grace Wolfe accompanied him to the student ex-officio conference at BOCES. “They were able to network with other ex-officio student board members from Southwestern, Maple Grove and Cassadaga Valley about their positions to learn more about what they are doing while serving as ex-officio members,” he said.

Also in his report, Sikorski told the board that the state Education Department is planning to de-couple the Regents exams from the graduation requirements. Beginning in January 2028, there will only be one diploma issued. The freshman class of 2028 will be the first to experience this, he said.

In her report, Elementary Principal Molly Anderson said that volunteer firefighters came to the school as a part of Fire Prevention Week. “I especially want to give a shout out to the third-graders who had no questions that the firemen asked that they could not answer,” she said. “This shows that they really take the information they are given seriously.”

Secondary Principal Andrea Marsh reported September attendance for Middle School was 94% and 96% for High School. She also noted homecoming was a great success with a lot of student and community involvement.

local.title: Council OKs fire contract extension
local.summary: The Dunkirk Common Council unanimously ratified a fire department contract that one council member called “a little complicated to us,” while the city attorney said it was just a matter of “switching the dates.” The pact calls for 4% raises for city fire department employees in 2027, and 2% raises i
local.body:
The Dunkirk Common Council unanimously ratified a fire department contract that one council member called "a little complicated to us," while the city attorney said it was just a matter of "switching the dates."

The pact calls for 4% raises for city fire department employees in 2027, and 2% raises in 2028, according to a copy of the council agenda provided to the OBSERVER by City Hall.

An emergency medical services training officer position is also added. The assistant chief position is removed from the agreement.

The agenda mentions the "switching of dates" that Elliot Raimondo referred to at the council meeting. It basically says the contract will now run from Jan. 1, 2025 to Jan. 1, 2029, instead of Jan. 1, 2023 to Jan. 1, 2027.

The agenda item says pay increases were zero in 2025 and 2026.

Prior to council's ratification of the contract extension, Councilwoman Natalie Luczkowiak asked for an explanation of it. "It's a little complicated to us," she said.

Raimondo replied, "We have an existing contract with the fire union... we negotiated with the state mediator for this (new) contract. Both parties came to the table with large proposal packets. The mediator ended up distilling that down to the tentative agreement we have from Jan. 1, 2025 to Dec. 31, 2028. Specifically, that agreement provides for modification of our current contract to change the dates... (it's) really just switching the dates to the 2025 through 2028 contract."

"I apologize for the complicated nature of it," Raimondo added.

local.summary: HOMESTEAD, Fla. Three-year-old Cooper held up a single finger. Yep, his dad was No. 1 again. Larson clinch
local.body:
HOMESTEAD, Fla. (AP) -- With the NASCAR Cup Series championship flag flying from a car window, Kyle Larson’s youngest child stood atop the No. 5 Chevrolet and signaled to everyone what had been known for hours.

Larson clinched his third Cup Series title in six years early in the 400-mile season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday. He became the first back-to-back champion since Jimmie Johnson in 2010; Johnson won five in a row beginning in 2006.

The 34-year-old Larson also became the 11th driver in NASCAR history with three Cup titles, joining a list that includes seven-time champs Richard Petty, Dale Earnhardt and Johnson. Jeff Gordon has four. Lee Petty, David Pearson, Cale Yarborough, Darrell Waltrip, Tony Stewart and Joey Logano have three.

“This was statistically probably one of our worst years,” Larson said. “To still come away with the championship shows how resilient everybody at the race shop is, everybody on my 5 team, all my teammates.”

Ryan Blaney won the race for Team Penske, passing Tyler Reddick of 23XI Racing with a little more than a lap to go and with NBA legend Michael Jordan watching from pit road.

“Congratulations to Kyle Larson … championship No. 3, two in a row,” Blaney said. “Those guys are awesome. Hopefully we can race with them next year.”

Reddick finished second, followed by William Byron, Christopher Bell, Bubba Wallace and Denny Hamlin.

The real celebration awaited Larson, who finished 12th. He immediately stopped near the start-finish line for a smoky burnout and then exchanged high-fives and hugs with his team, his wife and his kids. He climbed atop his car with all three children.

local.title: NIAGARA GENEALOGY: Genealogy questions answered
local.summary: Throughout the year I receive so many wonderful emails from readers sharing stories of family lost and found, sending encouraging words of thanks as well as SO many questions. I thought I’d share a handful of this year’s questions in…
local.body:
Throughout the year I receive so many wonderful emails from readers sharing stories of family lost and found, sending encouraging words of thanks as well as SO many questions. I thought I’d share a handful of this year’s questions in the hope of it helping other budding genealogists.

Can I find out everything about my family from online sources? Absolutely not. It’s estimated that only 10% of genealogical records are available online; the rest are in archives, courthouses, and libraries. Also, there’s nothing like researching ‘offline’. You’d be surprised what records you can find that you wouldn’t have known existed without an in-person visit.

Carol DiPirro-Stipkovits is a National Genealogical Society member, Association of Professional Genealogists member as well as a freelance writer. Send questions or comments to her at noellasdaughter@gmail.com .

entertainment.title: Tiësto Co-Founded Unlimited Productions Opens First U.S. Offices
entertainment.summary: The company launched its New York offices and announced plans to open an L.A.-based operation in 2027.
entertainment.body:
Unlimited Productions, the production company co-founded by DJ and music producer Tiësto , opened its first U.S. offices, it announced on Monday (Nov. 9). Located in New York, the new office is overseen by managing director and partner Jan Maarten Luijnenburg .

The company also announced plans to open an office on the West Coast in early 2027.

The expansion follows Unlimited Productions’ recent work in the U.S., where the company serves as the production director for Elements Music & Arts Festival in Long Pond, Penn. Unlimited built two stage designs for the festival, the Fire and Earth stages, and also redesigned the mainstage at HiJinx Festival in Philadelphia.

“For 20 years we’ve worked one way: we own every discipline, we draw every bolt before we arrive on site, and we treat our vendors as partners, not suppliers,” Luijnenburg said in a statement. “This year in the U.S. proved that model travels, from building Martin Garrix’s touring rig, designing the new HiJinx shows to bringing brand-new stages to Elements. No is not an answer for us. That’s where we do our best work.”

The launch of the New York office expands Unlimited Production’s footprint in the U.S., while the company’s European headquarters are located in Breda, Netherlands.

Unlimited Productions also built the production for Tiësto’s performance at the Pyramids of Giza in December 2025.

Jack van Deursen and Olivier Monod de Froideville first began the company, which was then named Livetime Productions, in 2005. It expanded into Unlimited Productions in 2009 with Bart Roelen and Tijs Verwest (better known under his stage name, Tiësto), and now serves as an “architect, general contractor and site supervisor” for shows and festivals, according to a press release.

entertainment.title: Joe Biden to Limit Memoir Promotion Due to Cancer Battle: ‘The Words Speak for Themselves’
entertainment.summary: The former president is set to release a new book, Promise Me, America , about his time in office on Nov. 17
entertainment.body:
Joe Biden will do limited promotion of his upcoming memoir , Promise Me, America , due to his prostate cancer diagnosis . In a statement on social media, the former president shared that his battle with the disease has slowed him down.

“Some days are better than others,” Biden wrote. “It hasn’t stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves.”

The book, out Nov. 17, details Biden’s time in office. He wrote that it “covers my years as President,” adding that the book describes “the challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them.”

“It’s about who we are as a nation,” Biden wrote. “What we stand for. And America’s role in the world. More than anything, it’s about my faith in the American people and the great American experiment in self-governance and democracy.”

He added, “While writing the book, I was diagnosed with cancer, a disease known all too well to millions of Americans and their families. My doctors continue to be encouraged by how I’ve responded to treatment. And the prayers and kind words and well wishes from so many of you have meant more to me and Jill and our family than you can ever know.”

Biden concluded, “Looking forward, I’m going to keep following what my father told me a long time ago: ‘Champ, when you get knocked down, get up.’ It’s a good lesson for me. And for America. We are blessed. America is the most unique nation on earth. Unlike other countries, we’re built on an idea. An idea bigger than any ocean. More powerful than any army. Stronger than any tyrant or dictator. That idea? All of us are created equal.”

entertainment.title: ‘A Photographer in Cannes’ Follows an Estonian Who Knows the World’s Red (and Black) Carpets – and Loved Getting a Vin Diesel Fist Bump
entertainment.summary: Erlend Staub, who is also the official photographer of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Fest, is in focus in the doc from Kullar Vilmne, which celebrates its premiere at Tallinn's 30th edition.
entertainment.body:
You have seen the stars and red carpet glamour of the Cannes Film Festival through the lenses of photographers, TV cameras and mobile phones. Now you can get a backstage look at the life and not always so glamorous work of one of the hard-working red carpet photographers in the new documentary A Photographer in Cannes , which world premieres in the Special Screenings program of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. Fitting the premiere location, the man taking the spotlight, while at the same time snapping pictures of the celebrities in it, is none other than Erlend Štaub, Estonia’s man on film festival carpets – both red, such as at Cannes and Berlin, or black, in the case of PÖFF . In fact, he has been the official photographer of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival for several years. A Photographer in Cannes comes from director and cinematographer Kullar Vilmne, who co-wrote the film with editor Erik Norkroos. The doc shows Štaub spending his days at exclusive parties, wild concerts and other events in Estonia, socializing and taking pictures, and spending his nights working on the photos to deliver them to the next morning. It also goes into the physical fitness, mental toughness and social skills needed to become a fixture of the world of glitz and glam. It is only fitting that the film also takes audiences to Cannes, which the veteran has attended for 15 years in a row, showing Štaub in his element on the red carpet and behind the scenes, where he is also shown running into Bella Hadid. Štaub took time out of his busy schedule to talk to THR about A Photographer in Cannes , share tips for aspiring photographers, discuss one of his favorite celebrity encounters at Cannes 2026 and which stars he would love to photograph in the future. Related Stories Movies THR Visionary: 5 Janusz Kaminski Shots Movies Janusz Kaminski, the Polish Cameraman Who Taught Hollywood How to See

How did Kullar, the director of the documentary, approach you, and what did you think when he told you he wanted to make a film about you?

First, I laughed loudly. Kullar texted me at six in the morning. I wrote him back, and I said it was not a good idea. And he told me, “Just listen to me. Let’s meet, and I’ll explain everything.” So, we met, and I listened to his idea. And I realized that the things that I’m doing are unbelievable to others. So, I said, “Okay, no problem. Do what you do, and I can help if you need help.”

entertainment.title: ‘American Idol’ star Justin Guarini endured dark spiral after Hollywood dream collapsed
entertainment.summary: After being dropped by RCA in 2003, 'American Idol' runner-up Justin Guarini overcame a dark period to rebuild his career on Broadway.
entertainment.body:
At the start of his career, Justin Guarini seemed to have it all: fame, fortune and a promising future in Hollywood.

After becoming the runner-up on the first season of “American Idol” in 2002, Guarini was thrust into the spotlight seemingly overnight. But when his Hollywood dream came crashing down, he found himself in a dark place that he would eventually come to view as one of his greatest blessings.

“I think it was one of the greatest things that could ever have happened to me,” Guarini, who recently released his book, “ Center Stage Confidence : How to Own Your Story and Command Any Room,” told Fox News Digital.

“Failure is the greatest teacher, one of the greatest teachers that we can have in any given situation because in that failure, you have one of two paths. You either give up or you keep going.”

In his book, Guarini recalled the moment he learned he had been dropped by his record label, RCA, in 2003.

“I stared at the TV in shock as my entire world came crumbling down around my ears,” Guarini, who said he learned the news during a “Weekend Update” segment on “Saturday Night Live,” wrote in his book. “Every illusion of fame, fortune, and glory fell away in an instant — only to be replaced by the silence of loss. In that moment, the veil of my arrogance, my assumptions, and my entitlement were lifted away, and I saw my life for what it had become.”

“I spent months playing my sad story on repeat,” he added. “I lost weight, slept more and more, and became less and less like myself, and the people who loved me started to notice and worry. I was living the ghost of the life I had always dreamed of and burning money and time in equal and absurd measure.”

As the first runner-up in “Idol” history, Guarini believed his future in the entertainment industry was secure. But his early success proved difficult to sustain.

entertainment.title: John Oliver Weighs In on Midterm Elections, Elon Musk and the Ultimate Southern Diss
entertainment.summary: “Democrats won so big on Tuesday it was sometimes genuinely hard to take all the positive results in," the 'Last Week Tonight' hosted said on Sunday's show.
entertainment.body:
John Oliver kicked off Sunday’s Last Week Tonight by running down a list of several Democratic wins from last week’s midterm elections.

The show started out with a blue wave crashing through the intro before Oliver cheerfully recapped the news: “It has been a busy week and, given the midterm results, a pretty good week too. Democrats won so big on Tuesday it was sometimes genuinely hard to take all the positive results in.”

He listed several big Democratic victories — earning loud applause from the audience after each — including the historically red Lone Star State: “It was genuinely hard to believe Texas had just turned blue.” Related Stories News Trump Says He Was Just Kidding About Making UFC's Dana White His Press Secretary General News Trump Reflects on Republicans' Midterm Losses, Reacts to J.D. Vance's Own Analysis in '60 Minutes' Interview

Oliver then turned his attention to a certain billionaire who spent a lot of money backing candidates who were ultimately defeated. “Then it hits you, Elon Musk wasted so much money,” he said. “The half a billion dollars he spent to try and buy the election just went up in flames faster than a parked Cybertruck. Speaking of which, we also learned this week he’s ending production of Cybertrucks, which isn’t technically an election result but kind of feels like one.”

Oliver also spotlighted the Mississippi Senate race between Scott Colom and Cindy Hyde-Smith. It’s still too close to call, but the Last Week Tonight host noted that Hyde-Smith “appeared to have prematurely declared victory” on Wednesdsay. Colom, he said, “had a quintessentially Southern response.”

Oliver showed a clip of Colom speaking to reporters. When asked about Hyde-Smith’s apparent gaffe, Colom paused for several seconds before saying, “Bless her heart.”

Explained Oliver: “If you are not from the South, you should know it is basically not possible to say anything meaner than that down there. ‘Bless your heart’ was essentially invented in the South as a way to commit legal murder on someone without getting out of your church pew.”

entertainment.body:
President Donald Trump reflected on the Republicans’ big losses last week with 60 Minutes correspondent Ross Douthat in his first sit-down interview since the midterm elections.

Douthat asked Trump for his analysis of what happened. “Well, No. 1, I was not on the ballot,” he replied. “But I campaigned hard for some people. And I think if I was on the ballot, it would’ve been a much different situation because you saw the level of popularity and love. There was love. We had massive rallies. You had to transfer those voters, however, to candidates that they didn’t like. But there’s something beyond that. They didn’t like the war. They didn’t like the fact that gasoline went up, ’cause I had it down at a low, and there’s a great dislike, incredibly, for Israel.” Related Stories TV Elon Musk Is Portrayed on 'SNL': "The Worst Thing South Africa Has Ever Done" TV James Talarico Crashes 'SNL' Cold Open, Apologizes for Texting Us So Much

Douthat asked Trump if he agreed with Vance’s analysis . “I don’t disagree with it,” Trump replied, adding: “He asked me what do I think. I said, ‘You write what you want.'”

entertainment.summary: We finally know who shot George Russell last season, and The Gilded Age EP tells TVLine that the shooter's identity was apparently actor Morgan Spector's idea.
entertainment.body:
HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Who shot George Russell? It's the biggest mystery left unsolved from the third season of "The Gilded Age," and Sunday's episode of the HBO drama finally gives us our answer.

The would-be assassin turns out to be Will Morris, the son of Patrick Morris, who took his own life back in Season 1 after a bad deal with George put him in dire financial straits. George's thugs pull Will kicking and screaming from his home at the top of the hour, though his mother Anne does her fair share of screaming as well.

This reveal puts all fan theories about George's shooter to rest; many viewers speculated that it was organized by his former business partner Richard Clay, but considering Patrick Page isn't set to appear in Season 4 , that wouldn't have made for a very interesting reveal.

"I didn't see all of the theories, but when we first conceived of it, we looked at the research and saw all of the different business stories that we could do," executive producer Sonja Warfield tells TVLine. "We created a narrative with a lot of open questions and suspects, because a lot of people were not happy with George. He was causing a lot of problems."

It turns out we have George himself, Morgan Spector, to thank for the conclusion to this storyline. According to Warfield, it was Spector's suggestion to make Will the shooter, an idea he had on set while filming the assassination attempt last season.

"It was Morgan who said, 'What if it was the son of the man who killed himself?'" Watfield recalls. "And I loved that, so I talked to [series creator] Julian [Fellowes] about it, and that's why we decided to do that."

HBO Though George comes very close to killing Will at the end of the episode, he ultimately decides to spare the boy's life, a decision that shouldn't be entirely surprising to longtime viewers of "The Gilded Age," says Sonja Warfield.

"In Season 2, there were people who were urging George to shoot upon his workers, but because he had that interaction with the one worker and his family, and he had gone to his house, that humanized him, so he didn't do it," the executive producer reminds TVLine. "Despite the laudanum, despite the rage, despite the fact that this person intended to kill him, there's a part of George that could not take a life."

You Can See Everything won everything it was nominated for at the 2026 Critics Choice Documentary Awards .

The buzzy Elizabeth Holmes doc , directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, won all five awards for which it was nominated at Sunday’s awards. The sweep marks the latest triumph for the A24 film and the first major award wins for the project, which debuted a little over two months ago with a surprise Telluride screening . It then received a high-profile screening at the New York Film Festival as anticipation grew for the documentary ahead of its Oct. 16 theatrical release. Related Stories Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued 'Cat in the Hat' TV Druski Embodies Elizabeth Holmes in 'You Can See Everything' Spoof on 'SNL'

Since hitting theaters, You Can See Everything has grossed nearly $80 million at the domestic box office , making it one of the highest-grossing docs ever, trailing Fahrenheit 9/11 and Everest domestically. Worldwide, You Can See Everything is a little further down the list of all-time box-office performers, but the movie still hasn’t opened in many overseas territories.

In addition to a best documentary feature Oscar nod , it’s been speculated that You Can See Everything could land best picture and supporting actress nominations.

At the Critics Choice Documentary Awards , in addition to winning best documentary feature, You Can See Everything won best director (Fielder and Oppenheim), best cinematography (David Bolen), best editing (Adam Locke-Norton) and best score (Ari Balouzian).

Fellow five-time nominee Once Upon a Time in Harlem also won multiple awards, three, while Ava DuVernay’s 14th , which went into the awards with a leading six nominations, was shut out.

Nuisance Bear , which like You Can See Everything and Once Upon a Time in Harlem was nominated for five awards, won best science/nature documentary.

entertainment.title: 5 Sci-Fi TV Shows That Were Canceled Before Their Biggest Mysteries Were Solved
entertainment.summary: Fans of these shows were left hanging on the edge of a metaphorical cliff. Here are off-beat series whose big questions remain unsolved to this day.
entertainment.body:
HBO Max Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Every TV fan knows the pain of a too-early cancellation. It's heartbreaking to know that characters we've come to know and love will never get the closure they deserve, or that we'll never truly get to experience the full scope of the writers' vision.

This goes double for sci-fi shows, which so often rely on mystery-box structures to keep viewers hooked. After all those weeks — or sometimes even years — of speculating, bouncing theories off friends, or discussing the show online, a disappointing finale can feel like a betrayal. But even a controversial finale is better than no real finale at all.

Unfortunately, the sci-fi TV shows in this list all fall into the latter category. But while fans will never have all the answers they want, that doesn't make the shows' twists any less mind-bending, or their questions any less captivating. If you can handle the frustration of an unresolved mystery, these five titles are worth a watch.

ABC Originally marketed as a replacement for "Lost," which was set to air its aforementioned finale the following year, the 2009 ABC series had massive, mysterious shoes to fill — and boy, did it pack in the mysteries. Starring "Lost" alums like Sonya Walger and Dominic Monaghan alongside other familiar faces in John Cho, Joseph Fiennes, and Courtney B. Vance, the show explored the fallout of a mysterious global event that caused the entire world to lose consciousness for exactly 137 seconds. During the blackout, people experienced visions — the titular flashes forward — of their lives six months in the future.

No one knew what caused the event, of course, but the unanswered questions just kept piling up. Over the course of its single season, the show introduced a quantum entanglement device that made its wearer immune to the flash forward, an enigmatic master physicist with multiple aliases, and much, much more. It even tacked on a whole new blackout in its Season 1 finale, which also left the fate of one major character up in the air. Unfortunately, fans weren't able to flash months into the future to see how it all ended themselves, as ABC announced the show's cancellation a few weeks before its finale aired.

ABC/Tubi Another member of the post-"Lost" sci-fi boom, "V" opened with a bold query. "Where were you when JFK was assassinated? Where were you on 9/11? Where were you this morning?" a series of text overlays read in the first few seconds of the 2009 ABC pilot. The show, a reimagining of the 1983 series of the same name, had lofty aspirations — literally. Like many of the best alien shows on TV , much of "V" took place in a mothership well above the Earth, where a race of reptilian extraterrestrials led by Anna (Morena Baccarin) plotted the planet's demise.

entertainment.title: 10 TV Shows To Watch If You Like SpongeBob SquarePants
entertainment.summary: "SpongeBob SquarePants" is one of the most influential cartoons of all time, and if you're looking to watch something similar, there are several great options.
entertainment.body:
Nickelodeon Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "SpongeBob SquarePants" has becomes a kids' TV institution at this point. It can take a while to get through its several hundred episodes, but assuming you do that, you might be wondering what similar TV shows you should dive into next, whether you want to relive your childhood solo or have something to watch with your own children.

"SpongeBob SquarePants" first debuted on Nickelodeon in 1999. Little did people know at the time that it would become a defining series on the children's channel. "SpongeBob" has outlived many of its contemporaries to the point where it's now one of the first original series still cranking out new episodes on the platform. As such, it's no surprise that "SpongeBob" is often considered one of the best Nickelodeon cartoons of all time . And it's not just because of its longevity; the quality, especially in the first few seasons, was unmatched by many shows of its era.

Even if you only stick with watching the golden era of "SpongeBob," which would arguably be the first three seasons, you may wonder what other shows capture that same zany, silly spirit. Fortunately, there are plenty of other cartoons to add to your watchlist that'll make you feel like a kid again.

Nickelodeon The only way something like "SpongeBob SquarePants" could make a splash on Nickelodeon is if you have "Rocko's Modern Life" laying the foundation of what kids' programming could be. "Rocko's Modern Life" is a hilarious Nicktoon where nervous wallaby Rocko (Carlos Alazraqui) just tries to get through the day with hilarious shenanigans ensuing.

But "Rocko" also pushed the boundaries of what kind of jokes you could put into a kids' show. There are many instances where this cartoon tells completely inappropriate jokes , like the name of a restaurant being Chokey Chicken.

But there's actually a more concrete connection between "Rocko's Modern Life" and "SpongeBob SquarePants." "SpongeBob" creator Stephen Hillenburg initially studied marine biology, but then acquired an interest in animation. After "Rocko" ended, Hillenburg pursued his own show, which would become "SpongeBob SquarePants" and define the channel for decades to come. entertainment.title: Nick Jonas Details What He "Resents" About His Diabetes

entertainment.body:
More than two decades after he was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, the Jonas Brothers member detailed his complicated relationship with the disease in an open letter to his “old friend.”

“How long has it been? 21 years. 21 years, and you haven’t changed a bit,” Jonas wrote in the letter, which is a part of Dexcom’s A Letter to Diabetes initiative . “It’s funny how often we talk. Every few minutes, honestly. Staring at my phone to see where my glucose is. Reaching for my pump to bolus because I’m about to eat something with 17 carbs.”

“Those are just a couple of the hundreds of little decisions I make every week,” he continued. “Most people never notice them. But they add up to a real relationship, because that’s what diabetes is. It’s an ongoing conversation between your body, your mind, and your devices.”

The “Burnin’ Up” singer noted that there are days it feels like he and his condition are “on the same team,” while on others it seems like his diabetes is on a “solo mission.”

As Jonas—dad to daughter Malti , 4, with wife Priyanka Chopra —put it, “In a lot of ways, that’s what family is like. You rely on each other, you push each other, and you know they’ll always be there.”

But when the “A Little Bit Longer” artist was first diagnosed with diabetes in November 2005 at age 13, its “unpredictability threw” him for a loop.

“I’d built my whole life around this unrealistic structure and belief that I was in control,” he wrote. “You took that apart over the years, bit by bit. Part of me is grateful I learned that lesson. Part of me resents you for it. Full stop.”

Jonas then admitted, “There are days I wonder what life would feel like without you.”

Elizabeth Fisher/CBS Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Robert and Michelle King's new smart, timely drama "Cupertino" is another success story from the TV writing duo, with snappy writing, a great cast, and storylines that feel like they were ripped from the headlines. Mike Colter and Rachel Keller play recently fired lawyers who start their own law firm to take on the tech giants of Silicon Valley and fight for the little guy. It's a David and Goliath story with a modern, technology-focused twist.

If you're a newly-minted fan of "Cupertino," you're probably (im)patiently waiting for new episodes to drop each week. In the interim, we've got some great recommendations to fill the void. entertainment.title: Timothy Olyphant's First Role Was In An Unaired Pilot Clint Eastwood Was Supposed To Produce
entertainment.summary: Timothy Olyphant's played everything from villains to leading men, but before he broke out, the Justified star almost got his start working with Clint Eastwood.
entertainment.body:
Kathy Hutchins/Shutterstock Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Timothy Olyphant's three-plus decades in Hollywood have brought him multiple Emmy nominations and opportunities to work with stars like Pedro Pascal, Drew Barrymore, and Walton Goggins. But early in his acting journey, Olyphant missed out on a chance to make his small-screen debut under the guidance of legendary actor/director/producer Clint Eastwood. Before he starred in his best shows , Olyphant's first official TV credit was for a 1996 episode of "Mr. and Mrs. Smith," but he was supposed to make his debut the year before on the pilot of "77 Sunset Strip."

Maria Bello, Jim Caviezel, and Vince Vaughn were slated to star in a reboot of the original series that ran from 1958 through 1964, but the new show's pilot never made it to air. Eastwood's production company was initially set to produce the show, but Olyphant learned at the first table read that Warner Bros. Television would be taking over production. The actor admits that he was just getting to know the entertainment business and wasn't privy to much information at the time. In a 2011 interview on NPR's "Fresh Air" with Terry Gross, he explained that "this was my first job of any kind outside of lifeguarding ... [Eastwood] was going to produce this show and I was going to be the kind of the Edd 'Kookie' Byrnes-type character." Kookie Byrnes was the goofy comic relief in the original series, which had plenty of high-stakes tension to defuse.

Crime City/YouTube Reflecting on the table read for "77 Sunset Strip," Timothy Olyphant shared, "I was looking for Clint everywhere. He's nowhere to be seen. So when we finished the reading I asked, where's Clint, you know. They said he quit." Eastwood is still listed as an executive producer for the pilot, along with "Mr. and Mrs. Smith" producers Kerry Lenhart and John J. Sakmar.

Olyphant also spoke on his early-career hiccups in a September 2025 episode of "Armchair Expert" with Dax Shepard, admitting that he actually bluffed his way into his first gig. "I had three things on my resume. They were all made up." He went on to explain that when the cast gathered for the first script reading, Eastwood was not present, and references to his company Malpaso Productions had been removed from printed materials.

When the star asked about Eastwood, he discovered that there had been a miscommunication between him and studio executives. There was "a long understanding with Warner Bros. when Clint would make a movie, he'd bring [the head of the film division] a script and they'd give him a budget, and then he'd go make it and they'd see it when he turned it in. Well, apparently the TV division didn't get the memo." Olyphant has picked up three Emmy nominations since the frustrating false start to his career and went on to star in genre-defining western series like "Justified."

entertainment.summary: Male solo artists dominate, though three female solo artists and two groups have also achieved the feat.
entertainment.body:
Morgan Wallen ’s I’m the Problem leads Billboard ‘s Top Country Albums chart (dated Nov. 14) for the 52nd nonconsecutive week. This ups Wallen’s career tally of weeks at No. 1 to 238, allowing him to extend his lead as the artist with the most weeks at No. 1 in the chart’s 62-year history.

Wallen’s achievement is especially impressive because he has amassed this hefty total of weeks at No. 1 in such a short amount of time. He first topped the chart a little more than six years ago — on Aug. 15, 2020.

I’m the Problem is Wallen’s third album to log a full year at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. Dangerous: The Double Album clung to the top spot for 97 weeks from 2021-23. One Thing at a Time led for 87 weeks from 2023-25.

Top Country Albums originated as Hot Country Albums in the Jan. 11, 1964 issue of Billboard . Johnny Cash ’s Ring of Fire (The Best of Johnny Cash) headed the inaugural chart. The chart was named Hot Country LP’s from 1968 to 1984, when vinyl LPs were king.

Twenty-one artists have logged 50 or more weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums. entertainment.title: ‘Steps’ Review: A Stellar Voice Cast Including Amanda Seyfried, Ali Wong and Bette Midler Gets Stuck in a Tortured Revisionist Fairy Tale
entertainment.summary: Stephanie Hsu, Nikki Glaser, Daniel Radcliffe and Peter Dinklage also feature in Netflix’s animated overhaul of the ‘Cinderella’ story, told from the perspective of her “evil” stepsister.
entertainment.body:
No doubt there are worse ways for families to kill a couple of hours together over Thanksgiving, but pity the adults forced to keep the kids company through Netflix ’s cloying, candy-colored musical fantasy, Steps . Simultaneously busy and sluggish, aggressively modern and tired, this charm-deficient Cinderella makeover squanders the considerable talents of a starry voice cast on lame dialogue laced with unfunny humor in a take on the classic fairy tale so convoluted that just following the plot becomes a chore.

Produced by Amy Poehler and co-directed by Alyce Tzue and John Ripa, Steps rehashes once-radical, now familiar tropes like the antagonist as hero and the bonds of sisterhood outweighing conventional romance. In other words, ho hum. The screenplay is credited to five writers and the story to six, originating with comedy folk duo Riki Lindhome and Kate Micucci, who go by the professional name Garfunkel and Oates. That outsize assembly feeds the impression of a project patched together by committee, sucking any spark or spontaneity or emotional uplift out of the material. Related Stories Business Netflix's Bid to Buy Radford Studio Lot Stalls TV 'Nobody Wants This' Renewed for Season 4 at Netflix Steps The Bottom Line Strictly for tots through tweens. Release date : Friday, Nov. 20 Cast : Amanda Seyfried, Ali Wong, Stephanie Hsu, Nikki Glaser, Daniel Radcliffe, Young Mazino, Peter Dinklage, Bette Midler, Damian Priest, Gwendoline Yeo, Matt Lowe Directors : Alyce Tzue, John Ripa Screenwriters : Ava Tramer, James Madejski, Jen Chuck, Dana Schwartz, Felicia Ho Rated PG, 1 hour 41 minutes

The central conceit is that Cinderella’s stepsisters are not evil, just misunderstood. Punky teen Lilith ( Ali Wong ) is determined to set the record straight on what she calls the “character assassination” of the storybook tale, carving out her own “happily ever after,” while her younger sister Margot ( Stephanie Hsu ) is too sweet and innocent to be tainted by that traditional lore; she loves everyone, especially frogs.

When their dressmaker mother Li Mei (Gwendoline Yeo) falls in love and moves them to the kingdom of Alouette, Lilith sees it as a place where she might finally belong. Mom’s new husband Edmund (Matt Lowe) is kind and welcoming, as is his cheerful daughter Cinderella ( Amanda Seyfried ), with whom they form a fast friendship. But the sisters’ cheongsams and black hair instantly mark them as outsiders in their macaroon-hued new environment, at odds with the prevailing 18th century French rococo aesthetic. The abundance of pink hurt my eyes.

sports.body: It’s finally Monday, which means the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings finally square off under the brightest football lights of Monday Night Football to close out Week 9 of NFL action. The Bills have struggled on defense a fair bit this season, while the Vikings have problems of their own on offense. Now, Minnesota turns to quarterback Carson Wentz again because starting quarterback Kyler Murray deals with a hamstring injury that has him listed as week-to-week. The Bills and Vikings have played just 15 times dating back to their first matchup in October 1971. Minnesota leads the all-time series 9-6, having won the last game between the two franchises. That 33-30 overtime loss for Buffalo came in Orchard Park, NY back in November 2022. Josh Allen is 1-1 against the Vikings since entering the NFL, with his first professional win coming in a 27-6 victory back in September of his rookie season in 2018.
