sports.title: Rams expect Terrance Ferguson to miss "another couple weeks" with hamstring injury
sports.summary: The Rams planned to have tight end Terrance Ferguson come off of injured reserve to play against the Commanders in Week 9, but he wound up being ruled out after Friday's practice.
sports.body:
Ferguson has been on injured reserve while recovering from an ankle injury and he suffered a hamstring injury at practice ahead of Sunday’s game. After the 20-13 Rams win, head coach Sean McVay said at his press conference that the injury will keep Ferguson out for a little more time.

“Pulled his hamstring . You can’t make it up, can you?” McVay said. “He was running just a standard out-cut, felt his hamstring pull and probably be another couple weeks for him.”

The Rams host the Cardinals in Week 10 and they have a bye in Week 11, so Ferguson will only miss one more game if McVay’s timeline is accurate. Even if it will take a little longer, Ferguson will have to be activated before his 21-day return window closes in order to avoid being shut down for the rest of the season.

sports.title: Baker Mayfield: Bears barked out the Buccaneers' cadence, causing a false start
sports.summary: The Buccaneers were flagged for five false starts on Sunday night, and quarterback Baker Mayfield said at least one of them was caused by an illegal tactic by the Bears.
sports.body:
Mayfield said left tackle Tristan Wirfs jumped when Bears players yelled Mayfield’s cadence, something that is a penalty when the officials notice it but is hard for the officials to know. Mayfield said he’s not sure what else the Bucs could have done.

“I don’t know,” Mayfield said. “The last one, I know they were barking out the cadence, which you can’t do that. It’s tough for the refs to call that because they’re not right there at the line of scrimmage. They called that on Tristan, but you can’t do that.”

That last false start Mayfield referenced came during a brutal stretch for the Bucs’ offense: Immediately after that false start, Mayfield was hit while throwing an incomplete pass, and on the next three plays Mayfield was sacked, although one of the sacks was wiped out by a penalty. The Bucs’ offensive line looked out of sorts, and Mayfield thinks the Bears’ cheating was a contributing factor.

sports.title: Jordan Love: Sunday's game "definitely up there" with best I've ever played
sports.summary: Packers quarterback Jordan Love ran for a touchdown to stake the team to a lead 100 seconds into Sunday's game in New England, but he used his right arm as his main weapon over the rest of the 45-27 win.
sports.body:
Love went 23-of-39 for 372 yards and three touchdowns with most of the damage coming via throws to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The two wideouts combined to post 17 catches for 335 yards and all three scores. Six of those completions covered more than 20 yards in the air and Love was perfect against the Patriots blitz, which led to the quarterback being asked if it was the best he’s ever played.

“Man, it’s definitely up there,” Love said, via a transcript from the Patriots. “It felt great. We’ll look at it, but it definitely felt like just a real fun game to be a part of, you know what I mean? When everything’s flowing, we’re putting up points, and everybody’s making plays, it’s definitely very fun to be a part of.”

Packers fans could be heard chanting for Love as the league’s MVP as Sunday’s game wound down and it was a performance worthy of those kinds of thoughts. If more of the same is accompanied by more Packers wins, Love should continue to hear such chatter well into the winter.

sports.title: Bears WR Luther Burden suffered a concussion on Sunday night
sports.summary: Bears wide receiver Luther Burden went for a medical evaluation near the end of Sunday night's win over the Buccaneers and head coach Ben Johnson updated his condition after the game.
sports.body:
Johnson said that Burden suffered a concussion. The injury came in the fourth quarter when Burden took a hit from Buccaneers rookie linebacker Rueben Bain after a catch. Burden fumbled as a result of the hit and the Buccaneers tied the game a couple of plays after Burden was helped off the field.

While Burden wasn’t around for the game-winning drive, he had helped the Bears’ cause earlier in the evening. Burden caught Caleb Williams’s second touchdown pass of the first quarter and had seven catches for 97 yards over the course of the game.

Burden will need to go through the concussion protocol before being cleared to return, but a bye in Week 10 will give him two weeks to do that before he’ll be at risk of missing any game action.

sports.title: Carl Granderson: Saints defense was disrespected, so we came in ready to play
sports.summary: Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders's response to questions about the Saints defense leading into Sunday's game drew the ire of Saints linebacker Carl Granderson and they remained on his mind after a 23-22 overtime win.
sports.body:
Granderson said before the game that the team would have a “ chip on our shoulder ” because of the smile that Sanders flashed when asked what he’d seen from the New Orleans defense. Granderson had a couple of sacks in the win and then opened his postgame press session by responding to a question about how much motivation the unit drew from Sanders.

“I mean, we seen a lot, you know, on film, so I do not think it was motivation. We saw them chirping,” Granderson said. “So we just came into this game ready to play. I think it is disrespectful for somebody to laugh at our defense, you know, take us as a joke. So we went out there and balled out. They had 2.8 yards in carry, and we stopped the run at 95 rushing yards on 34 attempts. So we did our thing on defense, and in overtime, the two-point conversion. So that was a good team win on defense.”

Sanders had his moments and the Browns would have won with a successful two-point play after a touchdown pass to tight end Harold Fannin in overtime. That would have likely led to a different response from Granderson, but the Saints made one last stop and they were able to get the last laugh as a result.

sports.title: Tee Higgins thinks Joe Burrow has "another step in him"
sports.summary: The Bengals extended their winning streak to four games against the Falcons in Madrid on Sunday and they continued to use their aerial attack to fuel their success.
sports.body:
Joe Burrow was 24-of-29 for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the 34-17 win and he has thrown for 1,215 yards and 16 touchdowns over the last four games. Wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been the main targets for Burrow and Higgins was asked after Sunday’s win if this is the best he’s ever seen Burrow play.

“No. I know he got another step in him, for sure,” Higgins said, via a transcript from the team.

Higgins said the same for the offense as a whole because there are things they could improve to find their “best form.” That prospect should be a chilling one for opposing defensive players and coaches as they try to draw up ways to slow down a red-hot Bengals offense.

sports.title: Malik Nabers: Fox tried to "create a narrative" about me being a bad teammate
sports.summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers took to social media on Sunday night to express his displeasure with how he was portrayed during the Fox broadcast of his team's 19-11 win over the Eagles.
sports.body:
In a post to his Instagram story that was later taken down, Nabers took particular issue with Greg Olsen’s characterization of him. After quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw a pass behind Nabers in the fourth quarter, Fox showed Nabers gesturing with his hands and Olsen said he was letting the quarterback know to put the ball in front of him. Play-by-play announcer Joe Davis said Nabers’s “body language has been terrible” throughout the game with Olsen agreeing that it wasn’t good.

The broadcast also showed Nabers slamming his helmet on the sideline at one point and sideline reporter Pam Oliver discussed Nabers’s desire to have the ball come his way. Olsen went on to say that there is “a fine line between being demanding” and being worried about your own touches that it detracts from the success of others. Nabers responded to what he believes was an implication that he’s a bad teammate.

“Y’all be trying [to] create a narrative on me soo bad, it’s actually crazy!! If you [don’t] like the way I play the game, keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE! But [Olsen] calling me a bad teammate when every team I’ve been on, there’s NOBODY I’ve played with has said dat bout me is crazy! My face the same way if I’m havin a good game, bad, winning or losing,” Nabers wrote. “If it’s a problem. 1. Keep the camera off of me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple.”

Nabers finished the game with five catches for 43 yards, which snapped a four-game streak with at least 111 receiving yards. He said in his postgame media session that he was frustrated with how the offense played at points in Philadelphia, but his frustration with Olsen and Davis might have been even greater.

sports.title: Ashton Jeanty had 5 catches for -5 yards on another awful day for Raiders' running backs
sports.summary: The Raiders' running back situation has been awful all season, but it hit a new low in Sunday's loss to the 49ers.
sports.body:
Ashton Jeanty, the running back the Raiders drafted with the sixth overall pick last year, had a historically bad game catching passes out of the back field, finishing with five catches for negative-five yards.

Yes, that’s negative yardage for the game. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins threw seven passes to Jeanty, and these were the results: incomplete, 3 yards, 3 yards, incomplete, -3 yards, -7 yards, -1 yard.

That’s the second-worst performance ever for a player with at least five catches in a game. The only player ever to finish with fewer yards was Jamie Caleb of the 1960 Browns, who somehow finished a game with five catches for -18 yards. It’s unclear how Caleb managed that feat, but Caleb finished his career with seven catches for -26 yards, so he was doing something spectacularly wrong when the ball was thrown to him.

And “spectacularly wrong” describes everything about the Raiders’ running backs this season. In Sunday’s loss, Jeanty was their leading rusher, with 25 yards on six carries. The Raiders’ other running back, Mike Washington, had six carries for negative-three yards. Between the two of them, Jeanty and Washington had 17 touches for 17 yards. One yard per touch is pathetic.

For the season, the Raiders have a total of 222 rushing attempts for 642 yards, a horrendous average of 2.89 yards per carry. They’re the only team in the NFL averaging less than three yards per carry. Nothing is going right for the Raiders when the ball is in the running backs’ hands.

sports.title: Caleb Williams: I could throw 100 picks and I wouldn't get gun-shy
sports.summary: Williams threw four interceptions on Sunday night but still led the Bears to a win over the Buccaneers.
sports.body:
Williams hit a wide-open Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain in the final minute of the game to set up a field goal as time expired on the Bears’ 27-24 win, and Williams said there was no hesitation to pull the trigger, despite his four interceptions. And he said he would have had no hesitation to pull the trigger even if Loveland hadn’t been wide open.

“I’m gonna throw until I can’t throw anymore. That’s how I live,” Williams said. “I work my tail off to be in this position. I’ll never not throw the ball. I could throw 100 picks in one game, if it comes down to it I’m gonna throw that pass that I threw to Colston, or if it’s a tighter window I’m gonna rip it in there. That’s how I grew up, that’s what I am. I don’t get gun-shy. That’s not me. That’s not my identity, not who I am. I’m gonna keep ripping it, keep ripping it.”

Williams admitted that he needs to find ways to get better, especially when the defense is blitzing him, but after the game he didn’t sound particularly concerned about the four interceptions. He’ll keep throwing confidently no matter how many get intercepted.

sports.title: Sunday Night Football: Bears overcome five giveaways, beat Bucs 27-24
sports.summary: Caleb Williams threw four interceptions, but the Buccaneers could not capitalize on the opportunities enough to win.
sports.body:
Caleb Williams and the Bears’ offense started out white hot, but an interception midway through the second quarter threw off the unit for nearly the rest of the night. Williams ended up tossing four interceptions — the most in a single game he’s had in his college or pro career.

But even with five giveaways — Luther Burden also had a fumble in the fourth quarter — the Buccaneers scored just 10 points off of them. Tampa Bay couldn’t turn a blocked punt into points either, despite getting the ball at midfield.

Chicago began the game with a 14-0 lead, as Williams tossed touchdowns to Rome Odunze and Burden. The Buccaneers got on the board with Chase McLaughlin’s 27-yard field goal in the second quarter before Cairo Santos hit from 25 yards to make the score 17-3 with 3:02 left in the half. McLaughlin drilled a 21-yard field goal to end the half, with Bucs head coach Todd Bowles explaining in his halftime interview on the NBC broadcast that he felt his team could score to start the third quarter.

That turned into reality, as Bucky Irving scored a 2-yard touchdown to cap Tampa Bay’s opening drive in the second half, narrowing Chicago’s lead to 17-13.

While Williams threw his fourth interception, Baker Mayfield then threw a pick of his own to Jaylon Johnson, who returned it 67 yards for a touchdown.

McLaughlin again made it a one-possession game with a 35-yard field goal with 11:24 in the fourth quarter. Then Burden’s fumble gave the Buccaneers the opportunity to tie it deep in Bears territory, with Irving scoring on a 6-yard run. Mayfield made the two-point conversion successful by scrambling up the middle to the end zone.

But even with the offensive challenges, the Bears got the play they needed to win it. Williams connected with Colton Loveland for a 38-yard pass all the way down to the Tampa Bay 16.

After running time off the clock, Santos sent the ball through the uprights as the fourth quarter expired for a 38-yard, game-winning field goal.

sports.title: Titans WR Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport
sports.summary: The Titans had a bye in Week 9.
sports.body:
Via WKRN, receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident over the weekend at Nashville International Airport.

“We are aware of the incident and are in communication with Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority,” the team said in the statement. “We will not be able to comment any further at this time.”

No details regarding the nature of the incident have been released.

The news comes at a time when Ridley has been the subject of trade rumors and speculation. He’s in the third year of a four-year, $93 million contract with the Titans.

A first-round pick of the Falcons in 2018, Ridley was suspended for all of the 2022 season for betting on games — including games involving his team.

He was traded to the Jaguars in November 2022. He spent 2023 in Jacksonville before signing with the Titans as a free agent in 2024.

sports.title: After Caleb Williams' fourth INT, Jaylon Johnson nabs pick-six off Baker Mayfield
sports.summary: Though they didn't score off a blocked punt in the third quarter, the Buccaneers did get another takeaway with a fourth interception off Caleb Williams.
sports.body:
Instead, Jaylon Johnson picked off Baker Mayfield and returned it for a 67-yard touchdown to push Chicago’s lead to 24-13 with 3:39 left in the third period.

Mayfield was clearly targeting Cade Otton on the second-and-9 play following an interception by Bucs linebacker Alex Anzalone. That’s part of why Johnson was able to easily step in front of the throw and dart back down the field.

Mayfield was effectively the only man to beat, and he got blocked as Johnson made his way to the end zone.

The Buccaneers have now picked up four interceptions and a blocked punt and scored just three points off of those plays.

sports.title: Video emerges of parking lot brawl at Raiders-49ers game
sports.summary: It remains to be seen whether the first Raiders game at Levi's Stadium in eight years matched or exceeded the 32 arrests made in the building in 2018.
sports.body:
Via Grant Young of the New York Post , video has surfaced of a brawl involving several people . Multiple individuals seemed to be rendered unconscious.

Fan violence resulted in Raiders and 49ers suspending their annual postseason game after the 2011 season. They play in the regular season at least once every four years, with the Raiders visiting the 49ers at least once every eight years.

It’s impossible to eliminate all fighting. When it happens, the goal becomes finding the folks who violated the law and holding them accountable. Deterrence is the only way to minimize such issues.

For folks who value their safety and well-being, scenes like the one that played out on Sunday are all the more reason to watch the games at home.

sports.title: Bucs score to start third quarter, trail Bears 17-13
sports.summary: In his halftime interview with NBC, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said that he didn't go for a touchdown to close the second quarter largely because his team was going to receive the second-half kickoff with a chance to double up.
sports.body:
Bucky Irving put a 2-yard run in the end zone, cutting Chicago’s lead to 17-13 with 11:37 left in the third quarter.

The score was set up by a 58-yard pass from Baker Mayfield to Tez Johnson.

That came after Mayfield had converted third-and-3 with a 7-yard pass to Chris Godwin.

It was a big boost to an offense that had scored just three points off three interceptions in the first half.

On the injury front, Bears defensive back Tyrique Stevenson is questionable to return with a hand injury. Chicago cornerback Kyler Gordon also went down on Mayfield’s deep pass to Johnson, holding his left arm as he came off the field.

Buccaneers safety Antoine Winfield is out with an ankle injury.

sports.title: Sunday Night Football: Despite three Caleb Williams INTs, Bears lead 17-6 at halftime
sports.summary: The Buccaneers scored just three points off of Williams' interceptions in the first half.
sports.body:
With a 14-3 lead in the second quarter, the Bears looked like they were about to go up 21-3, as they’d faced little resistance from Tampa Bay’s defense.

But on second-and-21, Williams was looking for Rome Odunze in the end zone when Tykee Smith stepped in front of the pass to pick it off. The Bucs gave it right back when Baker Mayfield was stuffed on a QB sneak on fourth-and-1 from their own 35.

Williams gave it away again on his next pass, when he heaved a downfield throw while getting hit. That pass was picked off by Zyon McCollum.

But again, the Bucs got nothing out of it, as they had to punt.

Williams’ third interception came on what looked like a throwaway attempt. But McCollum was able to pick off another with a dive, and the play was reversed upon review.

Chase McLaughlin hit a 21-yard field goal as time expired in the second half, as head coach Todd Bowles decided not to go for a touchdown with the clock stopped at :03.

That meant the Buccaneers managed just three points off of three second-quarter takeaways.

A week after not completing a single pass in a victory, Baker Mayfield is 11-of-19 passing for 139 yards with an interception. The Bucs are just 1-of-6 on third down.

sports.title: Kirk Cousins becomes an option for a contender, like the Vikings
sports.summary: With a switch from veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins to rookie Fernando Mendoza seemingly inevitable, the question becomes whether the Raiders will explore trading Cousins to a quarterback-needy contender.
sports.body:
At the top of the list, obviously, would be the Vikings, where Cousins played from 2018 through 2023.

The Raiders have pushed the implausible idea that they “ had not received any trade inquiries ” regarding Cousins entering this weekend. This time of year, the inquiries are rampant. Everyone is poking and prodding in an effort to see who’s available and what it would take to get them.

It would be malpractice not to make the call. For all anyone knows, the Raiders wouldn’t want much for him. There’s only one way to find out.

The Raiders also are putting out the word that they aren’t interested in trading him. Beyond the fact that there’s no reason to have interest if no one has called, it feels like an effort by the Raiders to operate from a position of strength.

Surely, there’s an offer for Cousins that they wouldn’t reject. By acting coy about possibly trading Cousins, the Raiders’ obvious goal is to make it known that it won’t be cheap.

If they’ll be pivoting to Mendoza in any event, why not trade Cousins? They have Aidan O’Connell, who has 17 career starts, to serve as the understudy to Mendoza.

That doesn’t mean anyone will make the Raiders an offer they’d accept. But it would be lunacy for a team like the Vikings, who have a Super Bowl-ready defense, to not at least inquire.

Chances are they already have. And, if they haven’t, chances are they will before Tuesday at 4:00 p.m. ET. Especially after getting thumped on Sunday in their return to the Bay Area.

sports.body: The New York Jets lost their fourth straight game and seventh of their last eight on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 - 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook. Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half. sports.title: Justin Herbert has a possible fracture in his left middle finger
sports.summary: The Chargers quarterback was injured in the fourth quarter of the 44-22 loss to the Texans.
sports.body:
The game was out of hand, but the bigger issue is Herbert’s hand.

Coach Jim Harbaugh said postgame that he made the decision to pull Herbert after an injury to Herbert’s left middle finger.

“It could be a fracture,” Harbaugh said, via Alex Insdorf of Bolt Breakdowns. “We’ll find out.”

Herbert appeared to injure his non-throwing hand on a sack by Logan Hall when the quarterback tried to stiff-arm the defensive lineman with 14:12 remaining. Herbert, who was sacked eight times in the 44-22 loss, threw a touchdown pass two plays later.

Herbert had his left hand surgically repaired during the 2025 season after breaking a bone in the back of the hand during a Week 13 game. He played through the injury and expects to play through his current injury.

“I’ll do whatever I can to make sure I’m 100 percent,” Herbert said after the game.

sports.title: Texans blow out Chargers 44-22 as C.J. Stroud throws five TDs
sports.summary: The Texans might not be back, considering it was the Chargers they blew out, but they can't be counted out just yet either.
sports.body:
Houston routed the Chargers 44-22 in a game that wasn’t that close.

The Texans have won three of their last four games, and they have the Browns, Colts and Ravens in their next three games. After beginning the season 0-4, Houston is 3-5. The Chargers fell to 0-8 and remain on track for the No.1 overall pick.

C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns, a 17-yarder to Xavier Hutchinson, a 63-yarder to Tank Dell, a 12-yarder to Kayshon Boutte, a 13-yarder to Nico Collins and a 63-yarder to Boutte. Boutte caught four passes for 125 yards, and Dell added four catches for 105 yards with the touchdown his first since December 2024.

Houston sacked Justin Herbert eight times, with Will Anderson, Sheldon Rankins and Jadeveon Clowney each collecting two sacks. Herbert injured the middle finger on his left hand on a sack by Logan Hall in the fourth quarter.

Herbert was 13-of-23 for 193 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Keaton Mitchell lost a fumble.

Herbert stayed in after his hand injury and threw a 58-yard touchdown to Quentin Johnston, ending a streak of 38 possessions without a touchdown. The Chargers’ previous touchdown came with 57 seconds left in the third quarter against the Broncos on Oct. 11 when Kimani Vidal scored on a 42-yard run in the 23-17 loss to Denver.

Ladd McConkey had back spasms in pregame warmups and didn’t play.

sports.title: 49ers beat Raiders 38-17, improve to 7-1 in 2026
sports.summary: San Francisco picked up five takeaways to beat Las Vegas in Week 9.
sports.body:
San Francisco beat Las Vegas 38-17 on Sunday with some strong defensive play.

The 49ers picked up five takeaways off the Raiders — intercepting Kirk Cousins three times and recovering a pair of fumbles from Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer.

San Francisco dominated the first half with three touchdown drives of at least 12 plays, building a 21-10 advantage at the half.

That lead got extended on the first play of the second half, with Kirk Cousins throwing a pick-six to linebacker Jaden Dugger to make the score 28-10.

The Raiders got back on the board with Brock Bowers’ 21-yard touchdown catch. But the fumbles from Mayer and Bowers kept the team off the board in the third quarter.

Las Vegas ended up with a giveaway on each of their last four possessions and five of the team’s last six in the contest.

Brock Purdy finished 17-of-25 for 232 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He also rushed for 40 yards on seven attempts before Mac Jones came in for mop-up duty late in the fourth quarter.

Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Bowers finished with seven receptions for 111 yards with a TD.

sports.title: Justin Herbert appears to injure middle finger on left hand
sports.summary: The Chargers quarterback left in the fourth quarter, but the score was 41-15 when he departed.
sports.body:
Herbert gave a stiff arm to Hall as he tried to get away before the 8-yard sack.

He got up looking at his left hand, which he had surgerically repaired in 2025 after breaking a bone in the back of his hand during a Week 13 game.

Herbert stayed in and threw a 58-yard touchdown to Quentin Johnston two plays later, ending a streak of 38 possessions without a touchdown. Their previous touchdown came with 57 seconds left in the third quarter against the Broncos on Oct. 11 when Kimani Vidal scored on a 42-yard run in the 23-17 loss to Denver.

He went to the sideline medical tent and emerged with a glove on his left hand, and, it appeared, a splint on his middle finger.

The Chargers did not provide an update on his injury, so it’s unclear whether Herbert left with his injury or because the Chargers were losing 41-15.

DJ Uiagalelei threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis with 4:19 left.

sports.title: 49ers DT Gracen Halton carted off with an air cast in fourth quarter
sports.summary: The 49ers have lost another defensive player.
sports.body:
San Francisco rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton has been carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s game against the Raiders.

A fourth-round pick in this year’s draft, Halton entered Week 9 with 15 total tackles, 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

On the other sideline, Raiders right guard Trey Zuhn is out with a concussion.

Mac Jones has entered the game at quarterback late in the fourth quarter for mop-up work with the 49ers ahead 38-17.

sports.title: Chargers score first TD since Oct. 11, going 37 possessions without one
sports.summary: The streak is over.
sports.body:
The Chargers went 37 possessions without a touchdown before Quentin Johnston scored on a 58-yard reception from Justin Herbert. It was the longest touchdown-less streak for a team — by possessions — since the 2024 Dolphins.

The Chargers trail the Texans 38-15 with 12:47 remaining in the fourth quarter.

Their previous touchdown came with 57 seconds left in the third quarter against the Broncos on Oct. 11 when Kimani Vidal scored on a 42-yard run in the 23-17 loss to Denver.

Herbert is 13-of-23 for 193 yards with a touchdown and an interception today.

The Texans have outgained the Chargers 460 to 240, with C.J. Stroud doing 21-of-34 for 384 yards with five touchdowns and an interception.

sports.title: Tomas Hertl scores twice as Golden Knights beat Sabres 4-1 for third straight win
sports.summary: Tomas Hertl scored two goals, leading the Vegas Golden Knights to a 4-1 victory over the Buffalo Sabres.

sports.title: Brock Bowers sets record for most receptions by a TE in first three seasons
sports.summary: Brock Bowers is good — really good.
sports.body:
Clearly one of the best young players at his position, Bowers has set another high-water mark.

With his 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter of Sunday’s game against the 49ers, Bowers became the all-time leader in receptions by a tight end in his first three seasons.

Bowers passed Trey McBride, who had 221 in his first three years.

Bowers has accomplished the feat in just 36 games, having missed five last year.

The tight end caught 112 passes as a rookie, 64 in his second season, and has 58 in his third season so far.

sports.title: Nico Collins' acrobatic TD catch gives Texans 31-9 lead
sports.summary: Nico Collins made one of the best touchdown catches you will ever see in the third quarter on Sunday.
sports.body:
The Texans wide receiver was tightly covered by Chargers cornerback Tarheeb Still when, in the front corner of the end zone, he somehow made a one-handed catch and got both feet in the end zone. Still immediately looked up to the replay board to see how Collins could have caught the ball.

The 13-yard touchdown has the Texans up 31-9 with 8:16 remaining in the third quarter.

C.J. Stroud has 286 passing yards and four touchdowns. His other scoring tosses covered 17 yards to Xavier Hutchinson, 63 yards to Tank Dell and 12 yards to Kayshon Boutte.

sports.title: Jaden Dugger pick-six puts 49ers up 28-10 early in third quarter
sports.summary: Things are starting to get out of hand in Santa Clara.
sports.body:
On the first play from scrimmage in the second half, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins fired a pick-six to 49ers linebacker Jaden Dugger.

Cousins dropped the snap before getting back up, looking to his right, and trying to fire the ball to Tre’ Tucker. But Dugger stepped in front of the ball and had an easy pick.

He then didn’t have anyone in his path as he made his way to the end zone, pushing the 49ers’ lead to 18 points.

sports.body:
Los Angeles has now gone 34 possessions without a touchdown. It has not reached the end zone since Kimani Vidal ran 42 yards for a score with 57 seconds remaining in the third quarter in an Oct. 11 loss to the Broncos.

The Texans limited the Chargers to 98 yards and held them to only three Cameron Dicker field goals of 52, 33 and 43 yards. They sacked Justin Herbert four times, including two by Sheldon Rankins.

Kayshon Boutte caught a 12-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud with 31 seconds left in the half, completing a seven-play, 76-yard drive that might have been the deathknell for the Chargers.

The Texans have 267 yards, with Stroud going 15-of-24 for 230 yards with three touchdowns and an interception.

Texans wide receiver Tank Dell scored his first touchdown since the 2024 season, 687 days ago, with a 63-yard catch-and-run down the right sideline. Dell missed the 2025 season and six games this season while working his way back from a gruesome knee injury that ended his 2024 season.

Dell has two catches for 66 yards and Boutte two for 47. Woody Marks has 26 yards on seven carries.

Herbert is 9-of-17 for 63 yards, with one of his favorite wide receivers, Ladd McConkey, yet to play because of back spasms during pregame warmups.

sports.title: 49ers dominating Raiders, lead 21-10 at halftime
sports.summary: The 49ers offense has been tough to stop all year and that has remained the case in Sunday’s game against the Raiders.
sports.body:
San Francisco turned long drives into touchdowns on each of the club’s first three possessions to take a 21-10 lead into halftime.

The 49ers got on the board with a 1-yard touchdown run by Christian McCaffrey. It’s his seventh consecutive game with a touchdown run, which is now the longest streak in a season in team history.

Quarterback Brock Purdy had a 1-yard touchdown run to put the 49ers up 14-0, finishing off a 13-play, 89-yard drive.

McCaffrey then had a 12-yard receiving touchdown, giving San Francisco three scoring drives of at least 12 plays to begin the game.

The only time the 49ers didn’t get going was in a potential two-minute drive, with the offense going backward on a sack and an illegal shift.

Purdy was 8-of-12 for 123 yards with a touchdown plus six carries for 40 yards with a TD in the first half.

On the other side, Kirk Cousins had the Raiders’ touchdown early in the second quarter with a 2-yard QB sneak. Ironically, that made him the team’s rushing touchdown leader this season with two.

Cousins is 6-of-8 for 48 yards. Ashton Jeanty has 24 yards on five carries.

sports.body:
Via NBC Sports research, Herbert is 0-3 for his career against Ryans as a head coach (twice) and as a defensive coordinator (once).

In those games, Herbert had three touchdown passes and six interceptions. Four of them came in the 2024 wild-card loss to the Texans.

The Chargers enter Sunday’s game on a 10-game losing streak. That’s one short of the franchise record, set in 1975 and matched in 2000. A loss today would drop the Chargers to 0-8 for the first time since 2000; that year, the primary quarterbacks were Ryan Leaf and current Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills (6-1) travel to Minneapolis on Monday Night Football to take on a Minnesota Vikings team that is also 6-1 and coming off its first loss of the season, 19-15 at Detroit. The Bills beat the Baltimore Ravens 36-10 last Sunday, but Baltimore lost both quarterbacks in the first half, and I’m careful about using that game as a measuring stick for this one. Minnesota is a different kind of test. Brian Flores is the main reason. His defense leads the NFL in scoring (13.3 points per game) and blitzes on roughly 70 percent of dropbacks. Carolina is next at 42.6 percent (the Bills themselves blitzed on 64.5 percent of dropbacks last Sunday, second only to Minnesota in Week 8, per Next Gen Stats). Josh Allen completes 65.7 percent of his passes against five or more rushers at 8.4 yards per attempt, so, on paper it’s a great matchup but the reality is that nobody is better than Flores sending 5 or more after opposing QBs. Buffalo has the league’s best offense (33.3 points per game) and the best EPA per play (0.175), and Minnesota has the best defensive mark (-0.189). The Vikings’ offense is their problem on the other side. It ranks 30th in EPA per play (-0.099), Carson Wentz starts with Kyler Murray out with a hamstring injury, and Justin Jefferson has 335 yards heading into Week 9, a lower pace than his career-low 2025, per Pro Football Talk. I think the game comes down to whether Buffalo’s offense can stay on schedule against the blitz while the defense tries to not give Wentz and Jefferson easy completions. sports.body: Garrett Wilson will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs today. Wilson is in the concussion protocol and will miss his first game this season. Wilson’s absence will be a problem for the Jets passing game in a game when they will need every weapon they can find. However, unlike past years, the Jets have some pretty good weapons even without Wilson, including rookies Omar Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq and young veteran Adonai Mitchell. Together with the return of Breece Hall to the lineup and the emergence of Braelon Allen as one of the best young backs in the game, the Jets should be able to compensate fairly well for the loss of Wilson. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Garrett Wilson Tim Patrick Blake Freeland Trevin Wallace Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Kohl Levao Joseph Ossai has been a disatrous free agent signing for the Jets thus far. He has missed all but three games with various injuries, and when he has played, he hasn’t been very effective. Signed for three years and $36+ million in this past offseason, Ossai has been a costly mistake to date. Perhaps he will eventually prove otherwise if he can just get healthy. Another issue on the above list is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. He has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. Unlike Ossai, health hasn’t been the issue for Wright. He just hasn’t been good enough to crack the lineup. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

The Raiders played a regular-season game there in 2018. That day, there were 32 arrests . It was the first time the 49ers had hosted a Raiders game since a preseason contest in 2011 that featured multiple incidents of fan violence resulted in a suspension of the annual low-travel-cost exhibition get-together.

Regardless of whether things get interesting in the stands, concourses, parking lots, etc., the game brings plenty of on-field intrigue. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan have a relationship that dates back to Cousins’s rookie year with Washington, in 2012. 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was Atlanta’s head coach during Cousins’s two seasons with the Falcons.

And Raiders coach Klint Kubiak was the 49ers’ passing game coordinator in 2023. Klint’s brother, Klay, has been the 49ers’ offensive coordinator since 2025.

The Raiders are unexpectedly in contention for an AFC playoff berth, at 4-4. The 49ers control the NFC West at 6-1, and they’re in position to force the road to the Super Bowl through Santa Clara.

sports.body: Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith had an expensive day in Orchard Park, NY last weekend. Smith received a heavy dose of fines for his on-field efforts against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. He was fined a total of $35,822 for two infractions, one against quarterback Josh Allen, and a second against wide receiver DJ Moore. The NFL handed Smith a fine of $17,911 for a facemask grab and tug he implemented on quarterback Josh Allen during a successful touchdown sneak, per Tom Pelissero. During the play, Smith was observed grabbing Allen’s facemask while trying to pull him back, then pulling and twisting the helmet aggressively until it ended up completely backwards — and with Allen’s head and neck turning almost a complete 180 degrees. Smith wasn’t penalized following the play. Here’s a closer look via still shots available from the play: [Image: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball in for a touchdown as Roquan Smith #0 of the Baltimore Ravens tries to make a tackle during a game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/gettyimages-2303585261.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Smith was also received an additional fine of $17,911 for unsportsmanlike conduct, which the NFL levied as a hit on a defenseless player. The Chiefs have lost two straight games after starting the season 5-0. Previewing this matchup, Maurice Elston, a writer at Arrowhead Pride, was kind enough to answer a few questions regarding the 2026 Kansas City Chiefs. - The Chiefs limited their opponents to 10 points or fewer in three of their first five games, but they have allowed a combined 48 points in the last two games. Are the recent struggles on defense just a quality of opponent issue, or are there bigger problems involved? I think there are some bigger issues involved, particularly the Chiefs’ inability to consistently pressure the quarterback and finish possessions on critical downs. Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs and controlled the ball for nearly 36 minutes. Denver only converted 2 of 11 third downs, so the defense improved in that area, but the Broncos went 2-for-2 on fourth down. That continued a trend we have seen against the Chiefs: opposing coaches are willing to be aggressive on fourth down because they understand the importance of extending possessions and keeping Patrick Mahomes off the field. The lack of a pass rush ties everything together. The Chiefs failed to record a sack against Seattle and produced only one against Denver. They have only nine sacks through seven games, with one of the NFL’s lowest pressure and sack rates. When you cannot consistently pressure the quarterback, offenses have more time to find favorable matchups. When you combine that with an inability to finish possessions on third or fourth down, it eventually leads to more plays, more yards and more points.
